notes:
### Added

- The Tescom Neoline, rack (RT) and tower: Find my UPS now recognises it on USB and shows its 24 V battery's real voltage and charge.
- A UPS that is just starting (its service, driver or USB connection coming up) shows "Starting up", with each step ticked as it comes, instead of an error and readings of 0.
- Recent voltage: hover the chart to see the input and output voltage at that moment.
- Actions → **Shut down this computer**, built in and off: when a UPS gets low, it asks with a countdown you can cancel (and a notification), or shuts down immediately. Preferences shows what it does. "Also when the app isn't running" lets the UPS service shut down even with the app quit.

### Changed

- Add a UPS → My computer is clearer: the UPS it finds shows as a card with Add, a newly plugged-in device is pointed out, and the help is behind the (?).
- Setting up a UPS plugged into this computer no longer makes it shut the computer down by itself: that is now up to you, in Actions → Shut down this computer. A computer set up by an earlier version keeps shutting down on low battery until you stop it from Actions. It also waits 2 minutes, not 15 seconds, before treating a UPS on battery that stopped answering as an emergency, so replugging its USB cable no longer shuts the computer down.

### Fixed

- Mac: Find my UPS reads the UPS on its cable. It asks for the administrator password once, since only an administrator may open a UPS's USB connection on a Mac, and stops early when it can't.
- Mac: setting up a UPS again no longer fails with "Bootstrap failed: 5", and no longer removes the app's UPS service when the app runs from its own copy of NUT.
- Adding a UPS that is already in the list opens it instead of adding it twice, and setting up the UPS on this computer again updates its entry instead of adding another.
- A UPS on the Leo/LiON/Neoline USB connection no longer stops being read after the computer restarts.
- A computer set up for another UPS model than the one now on its cable says so, instead of naming the old model.
- The beeper button no longer gives up on UPSs that take up to 30 seconds to report the change.
